note: Agents with a new mechanism, target or modality that are not yet approved for myeloma, selected from peer-reviewed early-phase trials and major meetings. Early response rates often fall with more patients and longer follow-up; meeting data are not peer-reviewed.

items.why: A third T-cell-engager target after BCMA and GPRC5D, given as fixed-duration therapy (about 12 months).
items.data: 324 patients, median 6 prior lines, 47.5% after BCMA therapy. ORR 42.1% overall; at the recommended 160 mg dose 44.3%, and 60.6% in BCMA-naive patients. Median duration of response 11.2 months.
items.safety: Grade 3–4 adverse events 59.6%; treatment-related deaths 0.9% (hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in 2, sepsis with DIC in 1).
items.next: Phase 3 CEVOLUTION: cevostamab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone vs standard of care (recruiting).

items.why: Engages two myeloma antigens at once, designed to counter antigen loss, a main cause of relapse after single-target T-cell redirection.
items.data: 147 patients enrolled. At the recommended 100 mg dose every 4 weeks, ORR 100% in 27 patients naive to BCMA and GPRC5D therapy; 55% in previously exposed patients across doses.
items.safety: At the recommended dose, infections 80.6% (grade 3–4 in 33.3%); two deaths from infection with hypogammaglobulinemia across the trial. Cytokine release syndrome mostly grade 1.
items.next: Phase 3 TRIlogy-4 (vs a BCMA bispecific) and TRIlogy-5 (vs teclistamab), recruiting.

items.why: A single infusion of a lentiviral vector creates CAR-T cells inside the body, with no leukapheresis, manufacturing wait or lymphodepleting chemotherapy.
items.data: 5 patients, median 3 prior lines: 4 responses, including 3 stringent complete responses; MRD-negative in all 4 evaluable responders by day 60. Median follow-up 6.0 months.
items.safety: Cytokine release syndrome in 4 (grade 3 in 3); all patients had grade ≥3 adverse events, mostly cytopenias and transient liver enzyme rises.
items.next: The trial stopped enrolling early in 2025 and the registry lists it as suspended; other in vivo CAR-T programs are in phase 1.

items.why: Donor-derived, gene-edited CAR-T cells available immediately, avoiding manufacturing delays and bridging therapy.
items.data: ALLO-715 (43 patients): ORR 55.8%; 70.8% at the selected dose and lymphodepletion, with median duration of response 8.3 months. CT0590, edited to resist host NK cells (5 patients): 3 responses, 2 stringent complete responses lasting about 20 months or more.
items.safety: ALLO-715: grade ≥3 infections 23.3%; cytokine release syndrome 55.8%, grade ≥3 in 2.3%. CT0590: no dose-limiting toxicity or graft-versus-host disease.
items.next: Phase 1 only; durability remains the main question.

items.why: A synthetic binder with a faster off-rate, designed to keep efficacy while lowering cytokine release and neurotoxicity.
items.data: 38 patients after ≥3 lines: ORR 100%, complete response 79%. Median PFS 30.2 months; 36-month overall survival 65% (median follow-up 38.1 months).
items.safety: At the recommended dose, cytokine release syndrome 94%, all grade 1–2; ICANS 16% grade 1–2 and 1 grade 3; no delayed neurotoxicity.
items.next: Phase 3 iMMagine-3 vs standard regimens (active, not recruiting).
src: Frigault MJ, N Engl J Med 2026

items.why: A CAR-T against a non-BCMA target, active after prior BCMA therapy.
items.data: 84 patients, median 5 prior regimens, 49% after BCMA therapy: ORR 87%, complete response 53%, median PFS 18.3 months, 1-year overall survival 90%.
items.safety: Cytokine release syndrome 82%, mostly grade 1–2; ICANS 10%; one death from cytokine release syndrome at the highest dose. Skin (30%), nail (19%) and oral (32%) effects, grade 1–2.
items.next: Phase 3 QUINTESSENTIAL-2 vs standard regimens in lenalidomide-exposed patients (recruiting).

items.ev: Phase 2 meeting data (not yet peer-reviewed); peer-reviewed preclinical and early clinical paper
items.why: A new epigenetic mechanism that evicts EP300/CBP from oncogenic enhancer networks in myeloma; oral, and active after T-cell redirection.
items.data: Randomized dose optimization with pomalidomide-dexamethasone (61 patients, median 5 prior lines, 66% after BCMA or T-cell engager therapy): ORR 69% at 20 mg, 54% at 30 mg and 33% at 40 mg in 44 evaluable patients.
items.safety: Grade 3–4 adverse events 71%, mostly thrombocytopenia (36%), neutropenia (34%) and anemia (20%).
items.next: Phase 3 DOMMINO-2: inobrodib-pomalidomide-dexamethasone vs standard therapy (recruiting).

grad.txt: Phase 3 SUCCESSOR-2 (Lancet 2026): mezigdomide-carfilzomib-dexamethasone vs carfilzomib-dexamethasone, median PFS 18.0 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.48); grade 3–4 neutropenia 61% vs 9%. Now on the landmark list.

Phase 3 EXCALIBER-RRMM (Lancet Oncol 2026): iberdomide-daratumumab-dexamethasone vs daratumumab-bortezomib-dexamethasone, MRD-negative complete response 41% vs 21%; PFS not yet reported. Now on the landmark list.
